newsitem.title: USA: Broad rally lifts Nasdaq 2.11 percent.
newsitem.headline: Broad rally lifts Nasdaq 2.11 percent.

text.p: A broad rally following favorable economic data spread to Nasdaq shares, pushing the index to its sixth-largest point gain ever.
The Nasdaq composite index gained 2.11 percent or 25.62 points to close unofficially at 1242.65. Advancing issues beat declining issues 2461 to 1656 on total volume of 583 million.
The Dow industrials surged about 179 points or 2.65 percent to 6962, while the long bond gained more than a point to yeild 6.98 percent.
"Nasdaq stocks followed the Big Board gains, which followed the bond rally. The rally was pretty broad, lifting even some of the smaller stocks, which have been left behind lately," one trader said.
Investors perceived the softer-than-expected Employment Cost Index as a sign that inflation was not a problem and that the Federal Reserve may refrain from raising interest rates.
Big winners included Intel Corp, which gained 3-3/4 to 150, Microsoft Corp, up 4-1/8 to 119, and Dell Computer Corp up 3-13/16 to 82-3/4.
Less fortunate was Network General Corp, which dropped 4-1/8 to 13-3/4 after one analyst downgraded the stock after its fourth quarter results signaled rising expenses.
